studies.label: Lab experiment: chatbot-avatar sketching with no support, Google Image Search, or Midjourney V4

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 Participants; random assignment in PDF p. 6, Section 3.3
counts_source.quote: We recruited 60 participants through digital student notice boards, mailing lists of university student clubs, and word of mouth.

arms.name: GenAI
arms.description: Paid Midjourney V4 through a private Discord server; participants entered text prompts and used the generated images as inspiration while sketching by hand. Tool tutorial before the task (PDF pp. 4 and 6).

arms.name: Image Search
arms.description: Google Images through an incognito web browser, with a tool tutorial before the task (PDF pp. 4 and 6).

arms.name: Baseline (No support)
arms.description: No inspiration support beyond the common design brief and example chatbot avatar; identical drawing materials and time limit (PDF pp. 4 and 6).

studies.task: Sketch as many different chatbot-avatar ideas as possible on paper in 20 minutes after viewing the same example avatar intended to induce fixation (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).

ai_tool.name: Midjourney V4 (paid version, via the Midjourney bot in Discord)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1: Midjourney V4 was the default model when the study was conducted (May 2023); its release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration identified in the full document.

estimates.outcome: Design fixation score: features copied from the example avatar
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Independent HCI researchers with design teaching/evaluation experience counted features copied from the example avatar. The normalized score divides copied features by the number of salient features in the example. The model uses the feature count with a binomial probit link (PDF pp. 5, 7-8).

regression.model: Bayesian binomial model with a probit link: DFS|trials(14) ~ Stimulus + (1|Participant ID) + (1|Image ID); GenAI coefficient relative to Baseline. Coefficient and interval are on the probit scale.

sources.quote: the boundaries of the 89% compatibility interval, often referred to as the credible interval.
The model suggests that the effect of GenAI has a 100% prob- ability of leading to higher Design Fixation (mean = .32, 89% CI [.11, .55]), and a Bayes Factor of 124

estimates.notes: The coefficient is the posterior mean. The regression.se field stores the printed posterior SD of that coefficient, not a frequentist SE and not an outcome SD; se_type is not_stated because the available categories do not describe Bayesian posterior uncertainty. The interval is the paper’s Bayesian compatibility/credible interval for the coefficient. outcome_scale=raw means unstandardized: the model field identifies the link or response scale. No participant-level outcome SD, standardized effect, or arm mean is printed. Design fixation is copying of a common supplied example, not similarity between different participants within an arm. It is retained as other, following the screening form; higher scores indicate greater fixation and less creative independence. The prose reports a 100% posterior probability of greater fixation and gives [.11, .55], while the table gives [.11, .54]. The tabulated interval is retained. test.value is the Bayes Factor supporting increased fixation. Participant and image random effects account for repeated sketches; the paper does not clarify whether raters were combined before modeling. Figure 6 has no printed values for the arm predictions or their error bars. Analysis-specific participant counts and contrast-specific observation counts are not printed and are left null. The study-wide recruitment count is not substituted for the number of people in this contrast.

estimates.outcome: Originality: rarity of each sketch’s category (total effect)

open_items: The paper does not print an analysis-specific participant N, explicit total arm counts, or a two-arm contrast N. Section 3.2 reports recruitment and a gender composition for each condition, but the required analysis counts are not inferred from these or from degrees of freedom.
No participant-level outcome SD or standardized effect is printed. The table SDs quantify posterior uncertainty in model coefficients, not dispersion of participants’ outcomes.

Table 3 prints a negative posterior SD for the GenAI total effect on variety. It is preserved with its sign in regression.se for audit, but is unusable as uncertainty until the printing error is resolved.

Intervals differ between tables and results prose. The extraction uses the tabulated intervals and preserves the prose values in notes and quotes. The direct-variety prose interval also has a malformed lower bound.
No numerical GenAI-versus-Image-Search contrast is printed. Arm-level predictions and error bars are figure-only; no values have been digitized or obtained by subtracting fitted coefficients.

The exact fluency response coding and normalization used for the variety figure require clarification. The screening form flags conflicts involving the printed sketch totals and plotted/model levels; no derived or digitized values from that form are imported.

The fixation model includes participant and image random effects, but the paper does not say whether the two ratings per sketch were combined before fitting it, and it does not print the fitted observation count.

Originality is a per-sketch rarity score referenced to other participants. The paper does not explicitly define whether its reference pool spans all conditions. It is coded novelty as in the screening form, without inventing a within-arm diversity estimate.

The separate supplementary study protocol mentioned in Section 3.1 is not among the located local files. The exact randomization procedure beyond the reported random assignment is not described in the available PDF.

Country of data collection and the Midjourney V4 release year are not stated. Author affiliations are not substituted for participant location, and the study year is not substituted for the model release year.
notes: One individually randomized, between-participants laboratory experiment; no unassisted later outcome is reported. The complete markdown conversion, including the appendix and references, was read in chunks. Tables, figures, and Appendix A were checked in the saved PDF, and all extracted numerical statistics were verified with pymupdf page text. No separate local supplement was located. Inventory of eligible results: the design-fixation GenAI-versus-Baseline model; total and direct GenAI-versus-Baseline effects for fluency, variety, and originality; and qualitative/figure-only GenAI-versus-Image-Search comparisons for each outcome. The direct specifications adjust for variables measured after assignment and are retained separately from total effects. All numeric coefficients come from one shared study and are not independent samples. Bayesian uncertainty mapping: regression.se retains the exact printed posterior SD, explicitly distinguished from a frequentist SE in every numeric record. No posterior SD is placed in an arm outcome-SD field. The reported compatibility intervals are preserved at their stated level without conversion. Bayes factors are stored as test.type=other, with test.value identified in notes; they are not p-values or standardized effects. Table rows in sources retain printed precision, including trailing zeros. Counts: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 states: Each condition had an equal num- ber of participants and was gender-balanced, with 10 women and 10 men per condition (gender was self-described by participants). The numeric arm counts are null because their totals are not printed, and analyzed counts are not assumed from recruitment. No attrition or exclusion of people is reported, but no creativity model supplies its N. Output corpus: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 states "all the sketches (N=277)" and "The process resulted in 83 clusters." These are the whole-study corpus and category counts, not participant counts or explicit model Ns. PDF p. 12, Section 4.6.2 states: For this analysis, we begin with the total set of sketches produced by participants in the AI condition (92 in total). This arm sketch total is not converted to a mean. Intercepts, shape parameters, and covariate coefficients are not treated as additional randomized arm outcomes. The tables are preferred over conflicting prose for the structured coefficient intervals. The prior screening form’s computed or digitized quantities were not copied. There is no identified shared sample in the screening form or paper. For specification selection, the total-effects originality record is the unadjusted novelty result; the direct-effects originality record is an adjusted alternative from the same sample. No outcome is explicitly preregistered or designated primary in the available paper.
